items.title: Q1 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Caroline & Commonwealth / Puritan Interregnum · Unit II: Poetry · John Milton, William Shakespeare
items.stem:
"What needs my Shakespeare for his honoured bones
The labour of an age in piled stones?
Or that his hallowed reliques should be hid
Under a star-ypointing pyramid?"
These lines are written by
items.explanation: These opening lines are from John Milton's 16-line epitaph 'On Shakespeare' (composed in 1630 and published anonymously in the Second Folio of Shakespeare's plays in 1632), arguing that Shakespeare's works are a more enduring monument than any stone tomb.

items.title: Q2 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: The Age of Chaucer (Ricardian 14th Century) · Unit II: Poetry · Geoffrey Chaucer
items.stem: Who among the following praised Chaucer's translation of Roman de la rose?
items.explanation: Fourteenth-century French poet Eustache Deschamps praised Geoffrey Chaucer's Middle English translation of the Roman de la Rose (The Romaunt of the Rose) in a famous ballade, hailing him as 'grant translateur, noble Geffroy Chaucier' (great translator, noble Geoffrey Chaucer).

items.title: Q3 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Post-War, Postmodern & Contemporary British/Irish & American Literature · Unit II: Poetry · Geoffrey Hill
items.stem: For The Unfallen is a book of poems written by
items.explanation: For the Unfallen: Poems 1952-1958 (1959) is the debut poetry collection of British poet Geoffrey Hill, containing celebrated poems such as 'Genesis' and 'In Memory of Jane Fraser' that explore history, martyrdom, and moral responsibility.

items.title: Q4 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Early & Mid-Victorian Britain · Unit II: Poetry · Alfred Lord Tennyson
items.stem: 'The Princess: A Medley' by Tennyson is
items.explanation: Alfred, Lord Tennyson's The Princess: A Medley (1847) is a long blank-verse serio-comic narrative poem telling the story of Princess Ida, who founds a university for women that men are forbidden to enter.

items.title: Q5 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: British Romantic Period · Unit II: Poetry · Percy Bysshe Shelley, Lord Byron
items.stem: Which of the following works is NOT written by P. B. Shelley?
items.explanation: The Vision of Judgment (1822) is a satirical poem in ottava rima by Lord Byron (published under the pseudonym 'Quevedo Redivivus' to mock Poet Laureate Robert Southey's A Vision of Judgement), whereas The Mask of Anarchy, Queen Mab, and The Revolt of Islam are all poems by Percy Bysshe Shelley.

items.title: Q6 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Post-War, Postmodern & Contemporary British/Irish & American Literature · Unit II: Poetry · Adrienne Rich
items.stem: In whose poem the readers meet Aunt Jennifer's tigers?
items.explanation: 'Aunt Jennifer's Tigers' (1951) is an early feminist poem by American poet Adrienne Rich (from her debut collection A Change of World), contrasting a married woman's domestic oppression under 'the massive weight of Uncle's wedding band' with the fearless, prancing tigers she embroiders.

items.title: Q7 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit I: Drama · Gurcharan Das
items.stem: Name the playwright who has written Larins Sahib.
items.explanation: Indian English author and playwright Gurcharan Das wrote the three-act historical prize-winning play Larins Sahib (1968, published 1970), portraying Sir Henry Lawrence, the British Resident in the Punjab after the First Anglo-Sikh War.

items.title: Q8 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: British Romantic Period · Unit I: Drama · Percy Bysshe Shelley
items.stem: Who among the following has composed the lyrical drama Hellas?
items.explanation: Percy Bysshe Shelley composed the verse lyrical drama Hellas in 1821 (published 1822) at Pisa, modeled on Aeschylus's The Persians, to celebrate and raise support for the Greek War of Independence against the Ottoman Empire.

items.title: Q9 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Elizabethan Period · Unit I: Drama · Thomas Heywood
items.stem: Name the playwright who composed the play A Woman Killed with Kindness.
items.explanation: A Woman Killed with Kindness (acted 1603, printed 1607) is an Elizabethan domestic tragedy by Thomas Heywood. In the play, country gentleman Master Frankford discovers his wife Anne's infidelity with Wendoll and punishes her not with violence, but with moral banishment.

items.title: Q10 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Post-War, Postmodern & Contemporary British/Irish & American Literature · Unit I: Drama · John Osborne
items.stem: Name the celebrated actor who played the leading role in the first production of John Osborne's The Entertainer (1957).
items.explanation: Sir Laurence Olivier played the leading role of fading music-hall comedian Archie Rice in the original 1957 Royal Court Theatre production (and subsequent 1960 film adaptation) of John Osborne's play The Entertainer.

items.title: Q11 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Age of Johnson, Sensibility & Pre-Romantic Transition · Unit I: Drama · Oliver Goldsmith
items.stem: Which of the following statements holds true in regard to "Sentimental Comedy"?
options: It is a dramatic composition which satirises the manners and affectations of a class.
It is a dramatic composition that focuses on characters, each of them representing a type personality.
It is a dramatic composition that depicts how seriously young people take love, and how foolishly it makes them behave.

It is a species of dramatic composition in which the virtues of private life are exhibited, rather than the vices exposed; and the distresses rather than the faults of mankind make our interest in the piece.
items.explanation: Option 4 quotes Oliver Goldsmith's classic definition of Sentimental Comedy from 'An Essay on the Theatre; or, A Comparison Between Laughing and Sentimental Comedy' (1773): a genre that exhibits middle-class private virtues and pathetic distresses to evoke sympathetic tears rather than satirizing vices.

items.title: Q12 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: British Romantic Period · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Jane Austen, W. Somerset Maugham
items.stem:
"I recognize that its heroine is a little prig and its hero a pompous ass, but I do not care."
About which novel of Jane Austen is this statement made by Somerset Maugham?
items.explanation: In Ten Novels and Their Authors (1954), W. Somerset Maugham made this remark about Jane Austen's Mansfield Park (1814), referring to its Quietist, morally scrupulous heroine Fanny Price ('a little prig') and clergyman hero Edmund Bertram ('a pompous ass').

items.title: Q13 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Late Victorian, Aestheticism & Fin-de-Siecle · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Robert Louis Stevenson
items.stem: In which year was R. L. Stevenson's Treasure Island published?
items.explanation: Robert Louis Stevenson's adventure novel Treasure Island was first published in book form by Cassell and Company in November 1883 (following its serialization in the children's magazine Young Folks from 1881 to 1882).

items.title: Q14 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Amitav Ghosh, Upamanyu Chatterjee
items.stem: Which of the following novels is NOT written by Amitav Ghosh?
items.explanation: English, August: An Indian Story (1988) is the debut novel of Upamanyu Chatterjee about civil servant Agastya Sen, whereas Sea of Poppies (2008), Flood of Fire (2015), and Gun Island (2019) are novels by Amitav Ghosh.

items.title: Q15 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Ben Okri, Olaudah Equiano
items.stem: Which among the following is NOT an American Slave narrative?
options: The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Oloudah Equiano
Life and Adventure of Henry Bibb
items.explanation: Songs of Enchantment (1993) is a magical-realist novel by Nigerian writer Ben Okri (the sequel to The Famished Road), whereas the narratives of Olaudah Equiano (1789), Henry Bibb (1849), and Solomon Northup (Twelve Years a Slave, 1853) are historic slave narratives.

items.title: Q16 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post-WWII · Sara Ahmed
items.stem: Who among the following theorists has written on affective economies?
items.explanation: Feminist and cultural theorist Sara Ahmed formulated the concept of 'affective economies' in her influential 2004 essay 'Affective Economies' and book The Cultural Politics of Emotion (2004), arguing that emotions circulate between bodies and signs to accumulate affective value.

items.title: Q17 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post-WWII · Roland Barthes, Paul de Man, J. Hillis Miller, Geoffrey Hartman
items.stem: Who among the following is NOT a Yale critic?
items.explanation: French literary theorist and semiotician Roland Barthes was not a member of the American Yale School of Deconstruction, which comprised Paul de Man, J. Hillis Miller, Geoffrey Hartman, Harold Bloom, and Jacques Derrida (co-authors of Deconstruction and Criticism, 1979).

items.title: Q18 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post-WWII
items.stem: 'Demythologizing' is a term associated with the works of
items.explanation: 'Demythologizing' (Entmythologisierung) was introduced by German Lutheran theologian Rudolf Bultmann in his 1941 essay 'New Testament and Mythology', proposing that biblical myth should be interpreted existentially rather than cosmologically.

items.title: Q19 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post-WWII · Antonio Gramsci, Theodor W. Adorno, Walter Benjamin
items.stem: Who among the following is known as a post-Marxist thinker?
items.explanation: Argentine political theorist Ernesto Laclau (along with Chantal Mouffe in Hegemony and Socialist Strategy, 1985) is a foundational post-Marxist thinker who combined Gramscian hegemony with post-structuralist discourse theory, whereas Gramsci, Adorno, and Benjamin belong to Western Marxism.

items.title: Q20 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post-WWII · Jonathan Bate
items.stem: Jonathan Bate's The Song of the Earth was published in
items.explanation: British ecocritic Jonathan Bate's foundational work of Romantic ecocriticism and ecopoetics, The Song of the Earth, was published in the year 2000.

items.title: Q21 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post-WWII · Louis Althusser, Theodor W. Adorno
items.stem: Who among the following is NOT a member of the Frankfurt School?
items.explanation: French philosopher Louis Althusser (1918–1990) was a leading structuralist Marxist in Paris, whereas Max Horkheimer, Theodor W. Adorno, and Herbert Marcuse were core members of the German Frankfurt School of Critical Theory (Institute for Social Research).

items.title: Q22 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit V: Language & ELT Pedagogy
items.stem: Which of the following methods is the oldest for teaching English language?
items.explanation: The Grammar-Translation Method (originally called the Classical Method, used for teaching Latin and Greek since the sixteenth century and adapted for modern languages in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries) is the oldest method of teaching English as a foreign language.

items.title: Q23 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit V: Language & ELT Pedagogy
items.stem: In the area of theory and research known as Second Language Acquisition (SLA), the classroom is considered
options: a site that always produces language learning blockade.
items.explanation: In Second Language Acquisition (SLA) theory and pedagogy (such as David Nunan's and Rod Ellis's classroom research), the language classroom is viewed as an 'experimental laboratory' where instructional hypotheses and learner interactions can be systematically observed and tested.

items.title: Q24 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit V: Language & ELT Pedagogy
items.stem: The arrival of corpus linguistics has revitalized
options: the writing that does not care for grammar.
the use of long sentences in newspaper reporting.
items.explanation: The arrival of corpus linguistics—using large electronic databases of authentic spoken and written texts—has revitalized the writing of empirical, observation-based descriptive grammars (such as the Longman Grammar of Spoken and Written English).

items.title: Q25 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit X: Research Methods
items.stem: Which of the following is one of the DON'Ts of writing a dissertation or thesis:
options: Compiling a bibliography as soon as the work is started.
It should be kept in mind that a dissertation or a thesis should take the form of an argument in which the writer must attempt to convince the reader of his or her case.
A researcher should not bother about the use of the proper scholarly conventions from the very beginning.
items.explanation: Not bothering about proper scholarly conventions from the very beginning is a major 'DON'T' in thesis writing; researchers must record accurate citations and follow consistent style conventions from the outset to avoid plagiarism and bibliographic errors.

items.title: Q26 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VI: English in India
items.stem: In which year, did the 'Indian Education Commission' (The sixth commission in the history of Indian Education) under the chairmanship of Dr. D. S. Kothari submit its report?
items.explanation: The Indian Education Commission (popularly known as the Kothari Commission, appointed in July 1964 under Chairman Dr. D. S. Kothari) submitted its landmark report 'Education and National Development' on 29 June 1966, recommending the Three-Language Formula.

items.title: Q27 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VI: English in India
items.stem: Who was the Chairman of the University Education Commission of 1948?
items.explanation: Philosopher and statesman Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan served as the Chairman of the University Education Commission (1948–1949), the first education commission of independent India, which recommended retaining English in higher education alongside Indian languages.

items.title: Q28 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VI: English in India
items.stem: Which of the following is the first newspaper of India?
items.explanation: Hicky's Bengal Gazette (or the Original Calcutta General Advertiser), an English-language weekly founded in Calcutta by Irishman James Augustus Hicky on 29 January 1780, was the first newspaper printed in India and Asia.

items.title: Q29 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VI: English in India · Thomas Babington Macaulay
items.stem:
"The great object of the British Government ought to be the promotion of European literature and science among the natives of India, all funds appropriated for the purpose of education would be best employed on English education alone."
Who made the comment given above?
items.explanation: This declaration—that British Government funds should be employed on English education alone to promote European literature and science—embodies Thomas Babington Macaulay's Minute on Indian Education (2 February 1835), officially enacted by Governor-General Lord William Bentinck's Resolution of 7 March 1835.

items.title: Q30 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit V: Language & ELT Pedagogy · Braj Kachru
items.stem:
Todd Kachru in "Three Circles of English" observes that English speaking countries are separated into three groups.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Central Circle, Middle Circle and Peripheral Circle
Primary Circle, Secondary Circle and Tertiary Circle
Inner Circle, Outer Circle and Expanding Circle
Inner Circle, Middle Circle and Outer Circle
items.explanation: Indian-American linguist Braj B. Kachru's influential 'Three Circles of English' model (1985) classifies World Englishes into three concentric groups: the Inner Circle (norm-providing native-speaker nations), the Outer Circle (norm-developing postcolonial nations like India), and the Expanding Circle (norm-dependent EFL nations).

items.title: Q31 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · V. S. Naipaul
items.stem: Which one of the following is false about V. S. Naipaul?
options: He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2001.
He won the Booker Prize for his novel A House for Mr. Biswas.
He contributed his stories to the Trinidad Guardian.
He won the Somerset Maugham Award for his Miguel Street.
items.explanation: V. S. Naipaul did not win the Booker Prize for A House for Mr Biswas (1961), which was published eight years before the prize was established; he won the Booker Prize in 1971 for In a Free State.

items.title: Q32 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit X: Research Methods
items.stem: Which one of the following is false?
options: An ideal literary researcher must be an insatiable reader.
An ideal literary researcher should not cast himself back into another age.
An ideal literary researcher should comprehend the current attitudes or the artistic assumptions.
An ideal literary researcher must have a vivid sense of history.
items.explanation: In The Art of Literary Research (1963), Richard D. Altick emphasizes that an ideal literary scholar must have a vivid historical imagination and the ability to cast himself back into another age; therefore, the claim that a researcher 'should not cast himself back into another age' is false.

items.title: Q33 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem: Which of the following is true in the context of New Criticism?
options: It follows the tradition of Historical Criticism.
The main law of New Criticism is that it should be subjective analysis.
The distinctive procedure for a New Critic is explication.
The distinction between literary genres does play an essential role in New Criticism.
items.explanation: The distinctive procedure of New Criticism is 'explication' (or close reading)—a rigorous, objective analysis of the internal tensions, paradoxes, ironies, and ambiguities within the text itself, rejecting biographical and historical criticism.

items.title: Q34 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Caroline & Commonwealth / Puritan Interregnum · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem: The pamphlet The Power of Love (1643) proclaiming the importance of brotherhood as a means of achieving a radical change in social relationships was written by
items.explanation: English Leveller pamphleteer William Walwyn anonymously published The Power of Love in 1643, advocating Christian universalism, religious toleration, and fraternal love as the basis for radical social and political equality.

items.title: Q35 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Jacobean Period · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose · Francis Bacon
items.stem: Francis Bacon's The Advancement of Learning attempted to draw a distinction between two kinds of 'truth'. Which are these?
items.explanation: In The Advancement of Learning (1605), Francis Bacon distinguished between two kinds of truth: Theological Truth (derived from divine revelation and faith) and Scientific or Philosophical Truth (derived from sense experience and inductive inquiry into nature).

items.title: Q36 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Augustan Age (Age of Pope & Swift) · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose · Joseph Addison
items.stem:
"I shall be ambitious to have it said of me, that I have brought Philosophy out of Closets and Libraries, Schools and Colleges, to dwell in Clubs and Assemblies, at Tea-Tables, and in Coffee-Houses."
To whom do you attribute this famous statement?
items.explanation: Joseph Addison wrote this famous mission statement in The Spectator, No. 10 (12 March 1711), declaring his ambition to bring philosophy out of closets, libraries, and colleges into clubs, assemblies, tea-tables, and coffee-houses.

items.title: Q37 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Age of Johnson, Sensibility & Pre-Romantic Transition · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose · Samuel Johnson
items.stem: Dr Johnson's Dictionary of the English Language was published in
items.explanation: Samuel Johnson's monumental A Dictionary of the English Language was published in two folio volumes in London on 15 April 1755, after nearly nine years of preparation.

items.title: Q38 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: British Romantic Period · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose · William Hazlitt
items.stem: An Essay on the Principles of Human Action was written by
items.explanation: Romantic critic and essayist William Hazlitt published An Essay on the Principles of Human Action (1805) as his first book, arguing against Thomas Hobbes that the human mind is naturally capable of disinterested benevolence through sympathetic imagination.

items.title: Q39 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Parallel 19th-C Tracks: American Renaissance, Realism & Early Indian English · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose · Frederick Douglass
items.stem: Which of the following is false about Frederick Douglass?
options: Douglass's autobiography belongs to the tradition of fugitive-slave narrative popular in the North before the Civil War.
He provides a first-person account of his life spent in slavery.
He was famous as an orator, dedicated to a black liberation movement.
items.explanation: Up From Slavery (1901) was written by African American educator Booker T. Washington, not Frederick Douglass. Douglass wrote three autobiographies: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass (1845), My Bondage and My Freedom (1855), and Life and Times of Frederick Douglass (1881).

items.title: Q40 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VII: Cultural Studies · Raymond Williams
items.stem: The phrase "structure of feeling" is attributed to
items.explanation: Welsh Marxist cultural theorist Raymond Williams coined the phrase 'structure of feeling' (in Preface to Film, 1954, The Long Revolution, 1961, and Marxism and Literature, 1977) to describe the shared, lived values and emerging sensibilities of a specific historical generation.

items.title: Q41 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Jacobean Period · Unit II: Poetry · John Donne, Adrienne Rich
items.stem:
'A Valediction Forbidding Mourning' is written by
A. John Donne
B. John Milton
C. Adrienne Rich
D. Sylvia Plath
E. Robert Frost
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Both John Donne (A) and Adrienne Rich (C) wrote famous poems titled 'A Valediction Forbidding Mourning'. Donne's metaphysical lyric (written c. 1611, published 1633) uses the conceit of twin compasses, while Adrienne Rich's 1970 feminist poem reimagines parting and language.

items.title: Q42 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Early & Mid-Victorian Britain · Unit II: Poetry · Robert Browning, Alfred Lord Tennyson, Andrew Marvell, Ben Jonson
items.stem:
Which of the following two poems are linked with each other in terms of form?
A. "The Last Ride Together"
B. "Ulysses"
C. "Upon Appleton House: To My Lord Fairfax"
D. "To Penshurst"
E. "The Waste Land"
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Robert Browning's 'The Last Ride Together' (1855) and Alfred, Lord Tennyson's 'Ulysses' (1842) (A and B) are both Victorian dramatic monologues; similarly, Andrew Marvell's 'Upon Appleton House' and Ben Jonson's 'To Penshurst' (C and D) are linked as seventeenth-century country-house poems.

items.title: Q43 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Augustan Age (Age of Pope & Swift) · Unit II: Poetry · Alexander Pope, John Dryden
items.stem:
Which of the following poems are written by Alexander Pope?
A. The Dunciad
B. Moral Essays
C. Grongar Hill
D. Cooper's Hill
E. Absalom and Achitophel
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The Dunciad (1728-1743) (A) and Moral Essays (Epistles to Several Persons, 1731-1735) (B) were written by Alexander Pope. Grongar Hill (1726) is by John Dyer, Cooper's Hill (1642) is by Sir John Denham, and Absalom and Achitophel (1681) is by John Dryden.

items.title: Q44 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit I: Drama · Vijay Tendulkar, Girish Karnad, Badal Sircar
items.stem:
Identify the plays originally written by Vijay Tendulkar from the following:
A. The Cyclist and His Fifth Woman
B. Scandal in Fairyland
C. The Vultures and Encounter in Umbugland
D. Sakharam Binder
E. Fire and the Rain
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Marathi playwright Vijay Tendulkar wrote The Cyclist (Safar, 1991), His Fifth Woman (2004) (A), The Vultures (Gidhade, 1970), Encounter in Umbugland (Dambadwipcha Mukabala, 1968) (C), and Sakharam Binder (1972) (D), whereas Scandal in Fairyland is by Badal Sircar and The Fire and the Rain is by Girish Karnad.

items.title: Q45 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit I: Drama · Asif Currimbhoy, Mahesh Dattani
items.stem:
Identify the plays written by Asif Currimbhoy from the following:
A. Princes
B. The Captives
C. An Experiment with Truth
D. Angkor
E. Dance Like a Man
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Indian English dramatist Asif Currimbhoy wrote The Captives (1963, B), An Experiment with Truth (1969, C, on Mahatma Gandhi), and Angkor (1973, D), whereas The Princes (1963) is a novel by Manohar Malgonkar and Dance Like a Man (1989) is a play by Mahesh Dattani.

items.title: Q46 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Elizabethan Period · Unit I: Drama · Robert Greene, George Peele
items.stem:
Which of the following are the plays written by Robert Greene?
A. The Famous Chronicle of King Edward the First
B. Alphonsus
C. A Moon for the Misbegotten
D. The Old Wives' Tale
E. King of Aragon
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: University Wit Robert Greene wrote the blank-verse play Alphonsus, King of Aragon (c. 1587, split here into B 'Alphonsus' and E 'King of Aragon'). The Famous Chronicle of King Edward the First and The Old Wives' Tale are by George Peele, and A Moon for the Misbegotten is by Eugene O'Neill.

items.title: Q47 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Edwardian, Georgian & Irish Literary Revival · Unit I: Drama · W. B. Yeats, Sean O'Casey, J. B. Priestley
items.stem:
Which of the following two plays were written by W. B. Yeats?
A. The Land of Heart's Desire
B. Time and the Conways
C. The Silver Tassie
D. The Countess Cathleen
E. The Plough and the Stars
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: W. B. Yeats wrote the verse plays The Land of Heart's Desire (1894, A) and The Countess Cathleen (1892, D) for the Irish Literary Revival. Time and the Conways (1937) is by J. B. Priestley, while The Silver Tassie (1928) and The Plough and the Stars (1926) are by Sean O'Casey.

items.title: Q48 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Post-Independence Indian English, Postcolonial & Global Anglophone Literature · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Chinua Achebe, Ngugi wa Thiong'o
items.stem:
Which among the following are true in the context of Chinua Achebe?
A. He wrote Arrow of God and Things Fall Apart.
B. His "Novelist as Teacher" is a seminal essay in the context of African Literature.
C. The name of the tribe he depicted in Things Fall Apart is Igbo.
D. He is a Kenyan born American litterateur.
E. He wrote the essay "An Abolition of English Department."
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Statements A, B, and C are true of Nigerian writer Chinua Achebe: he wrote Things Fall Apart (1958) depicting Igbo society (A, C) and Arrow of God (1964), as well as the 1965 essay 'The Novelist as Teacher' (B). Ngugi wa Thiong'o is Kenyan and co-authored 'On the Abolition of the English Department'.

items.title: Q49 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Elizabethan Period · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism · Philip Sidney, Stephen Gosson
items.stem:
Identify the correct ones among the following:
A. The Apologie for Poetrie was written by Sir Philip Sidney.
B. Sir Philip Sidney wrote the Apologie for Poetrie as a counterblast to Stephen Gosson's The School of Abuse.
C. Stephen Gosson wrote The School of Abuse in the euphuistic style.
D. Sidney's style was characterised by neoclassical restraint.
E. Sidney and Gosson wrote their critical treatise in the eighteenth century.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

items.explanation: On Heroes, Hero-Worship, and the Heroic in History (1841, A) and The French Revolution: A History (1837, B) ARE written by Thomas Carlyle (whereas Of Human Bondage is by Somerset Maugham, The Hour and the Man is by Harriet Martineau, and Hudibras is by Samuel Butler); despite the 'NOT' in the question prompt, Option 1 (A and B only) is the only option pairing Carlyle's works.

B. Thoughts on Parliamentary Reform
C. Past and Present
D. Explorations
E. On Liberty
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Past and Present (1843, C) was written by Thomas Carlyle and Explorations (1946, D) by Scrutiny critic L. C. Knights, whereas The Subjection of Women (1869, A), Thoughts on Parliamentary Reform (1859, B), and On Liberty (1859, E) were authored by John Stuart Mill.

items.title: Q52 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit X: Research Methods
items.stem:
Which among the following are true in the context of literary research?

B. It seeks to illuminate the work of art as it really is
C. It has no connection with the proffered information
D. It tries to see the writer as s/he really was
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: As Richard D. Altick outlines in The Art of Literary Research, literary scholarship is devoted to the enlightenment of criticism (A), seeks to illuminate the work of art as it really is (B), and tries to see the writer as he or she really was in historical context (D).

items.title: Q53 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit X: Research Methods
items.stem:
Which among the following are false in the context of autographical research?
A. These can be accepted on face value.
B. These are usually idealized.
C. These are coloured by compelling motive of the desire for self-justification.
D. These are embroidered through the sheer exuberance of the artistic imagination.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: In Richard D. Altick's The Art of Literary Research, autobiographical sources cannot be accepted at face value (making A false) precisely because they are usually idealized (B), coloured by a motive of self-justification (C), and embroidered by artistic imagination (D); Option 2 (B, C and D only) groups the three true reasons why autobiographical accounts are unreliable at face value.

items.title: Q54 · March 2023 (Slot 2)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit X: Research Methods
items.stem:

B. Not participating in any online information networks as others may copy the work.

D. Using online and printed sources to identify and locate material archives.
E. Peer management technique.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, C and D only.
items.explanation: Effective literary research requires having a comprehensive overview of relevant print and digital sources (A), critically evaluating online sources comparatively (C), and using print and electronic finding aids to locate archival materials (D).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Only A and D are correctly matched: John Keble's Oxford lectures De Poeticae Vi Medica translate as On the Healing Power of Poetry (A), and Harold Bloom wrote The Anxiety of Influence (1973) (D). items.explanation: In Anti-Oedipus: Capitalism and Schizophrenia (1972), French philosopher Gilles Deleuze and psychoanalyst Felix Guattari fuse Marxism (A) and Psychoanalysis (C) into 'schizoanalysis', critiquing both Freudian Oedipal repression and capitalist social production.

Are You There?

My father and I shove back the furniture
to the four walls of the sitting room
then lie on the carpet wearing blindfolds,
his left hand holding my left hand.

Are you there, Moriarty? he enquires,
before tightening (I imagine) the grip
on his rolled-up copy of yesterday's Times.

There is only one possible answer to that.
I give it while rolling away to the side
but still clasping his hand, still in range,
and sure enough he manages a direct hit.

Now it is my turn, but the moment I lift
my weapon I realise there is no reason
to continue. I can tell from his stillness,
and the chill and stiffness of his fingers,
he has been dead for a good while already.
— Andrew Motion

options: to create space for more furniture.
items.explanation: In the opening lines of Andrew Motion's poem 'Are You There?', the speaker and his father shove back the furniture to the four walls of the sitting room to clear space on the carpet to play the blindfolded parlour game 'Are you there, Moriarty?'.

items.stem:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows:

In this sense, one can think of literature less as some inherent quality or set of qualities displayed by certain kinds of writing all the way from Beowulf to Virginia Woolf, than as a number of ways in which people relate themselves to writing. It would not be easy to isolate, from all that has been variously called 'literature', some constant set of inherent features. In fact, it would be as impossible as trying to identify the single distinguishing feature which all games have in common. There is no 'essence' of literature whatsoever. Any bit of writing may be read 'non-pragmatically', if that is what reading a text as literature means, just as any writing may be read 'poetically'. If I pore over the railway timetable not to discover a train connection but to stimulate in myself general reflections on the speed and complexity of modern existence, then I might be said to be reading it as literature. John M. Ellis has argued that the term 'literature' operates rather like the word 'weed': weeds are not particular kinds of plant, but just any kind of plant which for some reason or another a gardener does not want around. Perhaps 'literature' means something like the opposite: any kind of writing which for some reason or another somebody values highly. As the philosophers might say, 'literature' and 'weed' are functional rather than ontological terms: they tell us about what we do, not about the fixed being of things.

What is the implication of the statement: "In this sense, one can think of literature less as some inherent quality or set of qualities displayed by certain kinds of writing all the way from Beowulf to Virginia Woolf, than as a number of ways in which people relate themselves to writing"?
options: Literature has values that are constant and universal for all classes and races.
Literature has a moral dimension, which cannot be superseded by any other values.
Literature has values that may be interpreted differently by different subject-positions.
The inherent quality of literature is its literariness.
items.explanation: In this excerpt from Terry Eagleton's Literary Theory: An Introduction (1983), defining literature by how readers relate themselves to writing rather than by fixed, inherent qualities implies that literary value is functional and interpreted differently across different historical and social subject-positions.
